name: Airbrush
summary: A pen-sized spray gun that lays paint in soft, even tones; with masks, it makes hard edges and smooth gradients side by side.
how: Build tone in 3 to 6 thin passes; each pass adds 20% to 40% of the final density.
Cut a hard mask for each edge that must stay sharp; leave the light soft.
Put one specular highlight of pure white on each chrome form.

origin.note: Abner Peeler patents a paint distributor; the airbrush of Charles Burdick (1893) goes into photo studios for retouch.

adoptions.via: Streamline posters and car advertisements use airbrushed gradients and chrome.
Illustrators airbrush surreal chrome, lightning and X-ray cut-aways for album covers and magazines.
Photoshop 1.0 ships with an airbrush tool, and the soft spray becomes digital.
Glossy interface gradients and highlights take the airbrush look to the screen.

sources.title: Seng-gye Tombs Curtis and Christopher Hunt, The Airbrush Book (1980)
